From 5ad6af5c91e9b942c44b657122270d935db3a813 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Feb 2024 15:17:14 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/xe: Assume large page size if VMA not yet bound

The calculation to determine max page size of a VMA during a REMAP
operations assumes the VMA has been bound. This assumption is not true
if the VMA is from an eariler operation in an array of binds. If a VMA
has not been bound use the maximum page size which will ensure the
previous / next REMAP operations are not incorrectly skipped.

Fixes: 8f33b4f054fc ("drm/xe: Avoid doing rebinds")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240205231714.2956225-1-matthew.brost@intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c
index 7e29b816c4d4..ed594fa2f8da 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c
@@ -2200,8 +2200,10 @@ static u64 xe_vma_max_pte_size(struct xe_vma *vma)
 		return SZ_1G;
 	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_2M)
 		return SZ_2M;
+	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_4K)
+		return SZ_4K;
 
-	return SZ_4K;
+	return SZ_1G;	/* Uninitialized, used max size */
 }
 
 static u64 xe_vma_set_pte_size(struct xe_vma *vma, u64 size)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c`**
   - The function `xe_vma_max_pte_size` has been modified to include an additional condition that checks if the `vma->gpuva.flags` has the `XE_VMA_PTE_4K` flag set. If this condition is true, the function now returns `SZ_4K`.
   - The default return value for the case when the VMA is uninitialized has been changed from `SZ_4K` to `SZ_1G`, ensuring that the maximum page size is used when the VMA has not been bound.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes in `xe_vm.c` address a bug related to the assumption that a Virtual Memory Area (VMA) is bound during REMAP operations. By adding the check for the `XE_VMA_PTE_4K` flag and adjusting the default return value, the patch ensures that if a VMA is not bound, the maximum page size is used. This prevents potential issues where previous or next REMAP operations could be incorrectly skipped, thereby improving the reliability of the memory management in the driver. The modifications are directly related to fixing the bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the Fixes tag).

Here is the commit message:
drm/xe: Assume large page size if VMA not yet bound

The calculation to determine max page size of a VMA during a REMAP
operations assumes the VMA has been bound. This assumption is not true
if the VMA is from an eariler operation in an array of binds. If a VMA
has not been bound use the maximum page size which will ensure the
previous / next REMAP operations are not incorrectly skipped.

Fixes: 8f33b4f054fc ("drm/xe: Avoid doing rebinds")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240205231714.2956225-1-matthew.brost@intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the incorrect assumption that a Virtual Memory Area (VMA) is always bound during REMAP operations. When a VMA is not yet bound, the calculation for the maximum page size defaults to a smaller size (SZ_4K), which can lead to skipping necessary REMAP operations. This can occur particularly when the VMA is from an earlier operation in an array of binds, resulting in improper memory management.

Here is the patch:
 
 static u64 xe_vma_max_pte_size(struct xe_vma *vma)
 {
 	if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_1G)
 		return SZ_1G;
 	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_2M)
 		return SZ_2M;
+	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_4K)
+		return SZ_4K;
 
-	return SZ_4K;
+	return SZ_1G;	/* Uninitialized, used max size */
 }
